To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

parton energy loss leads to a strong nuclear suppression of dihadron ratios in deep-inelastic scattering and a mild enhancement of near-side correlations with increasing centrality in high-energy heavy-ion collision.

the nuclear modification of dihadrons in DIS and heavy ion collisions is dominated by the medium modification of the single hadron fragmentation function, which in turn is dominated by partonic energy loss.

the medium modification of dihadrons in DIS and heavy-ion collisions can be understood as a consequence of gluon bremsstahlung, and that the medium modification for dihadron fragmentation can be understood as an extension of that for single-hadron fragmentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the quark and gluon dynamics in dense matter and the associated medium effects on the hadronization process.
the modification of jet fragmentation in hot and nuclear medium.
the modification of hadronization in hot and dense matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the medium modification of dihadrons is a consequence of the parton energy loss, which is the same mechanism for the single hadrons.
jet modification is a direct consequence of multiple partonic scattering, and that the medium-induced partonic energy loss is a key factor in jet quenching in dense QCD matter.
the observed medium modification in both DIS and AA collisions is due to the parton energy loss in the medium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
jet-medium interactions in hot and nuclear medium are very similar.

parton energy loss, as the dominant mechanism of medium modification of jet fragmentation functions in hot/dense QCD matter, can be studied in detail through measurements of multihadron observales in both DIS and heavy-ion experiments, and that the twist expansion of fragmentation functions is a useful tool for studying partonic energy loss in dense matter.

jet-medium interaction in dense matter can be well described by the twist expansion, which is based on a systematic power expansion of the jet-medium interaction strength in terms of a small parameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modification of dihadrons in heavy-ion collisions can be understood by the modification of single hadrons.
parton energy loss is a universal process in dense matter, and the same theoretical framework is applicable in both DIS off large nuclei and heavy-ion collisions.
parton energy loss can be reliably extracted from dihadron fragmentation function ratios.
